name: Grýla
description: The Icelandic ogress who comes down from the mountains at Christmas to cook naughty children

debut.title: Icelandic sagas and folk tradition
debut.era: named as a troll in 13th-century Icelandic writing

legend: Grýla lives in a cave in the mountains, and every Christmas she comes down to the farms looking for children who have misbehaved. She stuffs them in her sack and takes them home to boil in her pot, a stew she's very fond of. She's an old figure: her name turns up as a troll's in Icelandic writing of the 1200s. Later folklore gave her a lazy husband, Leppalúði, thirteen mischievous sons, the Yule Lads, and a giant pet, the Yule Cat. She and her sons became so frightening that in 1746 the authorities issued a decree against parents using them to scare children.

myths.claim: Grýla is the mother of the Yule Lads.
myths.explanation: The thirteen Yule Lads are her sons, usually with her husband Leppalúði.
Her name appears as a troll's in Icelandic writing of the 1200s. The Christmas role came later.

myths.claim: Grýla only eats children who misbehave.
myths.explanation: Good children are safe. The naughty ones go in the sack, and then the pot.

weaknesses: A long walk from the mountains
legacy: Countless Icelandic poems and songs about Grýla and her family
The 1746 decree against frightening children with the Yule Lads
facts: Grýla is a child-eating ogress from Icelandic folklore

hostIntro: Our guest tonight runs a family business: thirteen sons, one cat and a very big pot. Don't ask what's in the stew.
